notes: Current Marsannay vineyard law. Common geometry, density, irrigation and dead/missing-vine rules apply across the appellation. Red and white pruning/crop-load paths are executable with the current vineyard-management schema. Rosé pruning and its 10,500 kg/ha crop-load ceiling are sourced but deliberately left unresolved until 'rose' is a first-class vineyard-management style; the engine must not borrow the red 9,000 kg/ha limit.

constraints.notes: Current reviewed Marsannay vineyard law. Density is at least 9,000 vines/ha; conventional rows are at most 1.25 m apart with at least 0.50 m between vines; plantation en foule requires strictly more than 0.50 m between vines and individual stakes. Irrigation is prohibited. Ordinary red pruning is capped at eight buds per vine for the listed systems. White Royat/bilateral cordon permits ten buds and white Guyot simple eight. Chablis pruning is Chardonnay-specific and is therefore withheld from the positive generic white path until pruning legality can depend on grape identity. Guyot double is permitted only during the two-year cordon-establishment period and remains unresolved. Extra retained buds require a compliant observed fruiting-shoot count at 11-12 leaves. Trellised canopy height is at least 0.6 times row spacing. Parcel crop load is capped at 9,000 kg/ha for red and 10,500 for white; the separately sourced rosé 10,500 kg/ha path is not generalized while the management enum is red/white-only. The 20% dead/missing-vine trigger feeds the national D.645-4 proportional-yield remedy.
